source_text: Generalizability debates underscore the trials' restriction to high-prevalence (3–20% adult HIV), low-circumcision (<10%) sub-Saharan African settings among monogamous or low-partner-count men, limiting extrapolation to low-prevalence regions, female-to-male transmission assumptions, or populations with diverse sexual networks; observational data from diverse ecologies often yield weaker or null associations, prompting arguments that RCTs overestimate population-level causal effects absent real-world confounders like variable surgical quality or uptake barriers. [100]
